correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge2\), the torus-gradient equations and line-pencil restrictions exhaust all singular points. The analytic branches at either nonordinary vertex arise from the distinct simple roots of \(\rho^m=-1\) and the implicit-function theorem; each matched contact is exactly \(m+1\), and all cross-group contacts are one. The branch formula gives \(\delta=3m^2-m\) and \(\mu=6m^2-4m+1\). The complete embedded resolution has a central multiplicity-\(2m\) component with \(m\) tails of length \(m\) and multiplicities \(2m+2k\), with punctured Euler characteristics \(2-m\), zero, and \(-1\). A’Campo gives the claimed monodromy characteristic polynomial, whose degree equals \(\mu\). Two polynomial syzygies and the exact determinant \(-4f\) establish freeness via Saito’s criterion and hence total Tjurina number. Subtracting node and ordinary-multiple-point contributions yields \(\tau=5m^2-2m\) at each exceptional vertex and the global defect. The saved exact checker replayed both universal algebraic identities, the determinant, and finite consistency tests; the analytic resolution—not finite sampling—establishes the infinite assertion.
